The @NVIDIA event in London was fantastic from many perspectives.

Firstly, because it allowed me to talk to countless people and finally discuss the future of AI outside of social media, and in places where Jensen Huang also shared his perspective.

Secondly, because it's incredibly exciting to see that the Build-a-Claw events accomplish two things simultaneously: teaching beginners the first steps in setting up agents in OpenClaw or Hermes, and maximizing the benefits for advanced users. Given that agentic AI is undoubtedly the future, we need more events like this to lower the barrier to entry for beginners.

My journey continues, though. Today and tomorrow I'll be visiting other countries and staying in close contact with them. First Paris, then London, and, well, there's more to come. Much more :) (some impressions in the comment section)

White Circle's RISE found new ways to bypass the safety filters of OpenAI and Google's image models.

Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, the system evolves reusable attack strategies and checks its automated scoring against human labels.

In the paper's nudity tests, the team reports human-confirmed success rates of 13.33% for DALL-E 3, 9.47% for Nano Banana 2 and 3.27% for GPT-Image-2 with default moderation. Each prompt got three attempts; one confirmed violation counted as a success.

Several earlier methods fell to near zero under the same stricter evaluation.

Reusing old jailbreaks can make a model's defenses look stronger than they actually are. RISE gives researchers a way to keep searching for weaknesses as those defenses change.

I believe the scenario outlined by Sam Altman is unrealistic and will not come to pass. No one would entrust an AI with overall political responsibility solely based on the belief that it is intelligent enough to make the right decisions- especially not when that intelligence is no longer understood.

While the consequences would indeed be difficult to foresee, that is precisely why the scenario is unlikely. It is certainly probable that AI will support political processes or even make decisions independently; however, handing over control to an AI in the sense of a presidential-style rule is far-fetched. https://t.co/mvcPQrAPXE
